newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Electro Magnetics in S$88 mln rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Electro Magnetics in S$88 mln rescue plan.

text.p: Price Waterhouse, judicial managers for ailing video cassette maker Electro Magnetics (1992) Ltd, said on Monday they had reached a provisional agreement to sell the company in a deal worth Singapore $88 million.
Shareholders are expected to get 16.8 cents per share if the plan goes through, the judicial managers said.
The potential rescuer was named by Price Waterhouse as businessman Joseph Gondobintoro, a Singapore permanent resident with extensive Indonesian business interests.
He has made a S$3 million deposit in letters of credit to signify his intentions, the judicial managers said.
It is not expected that the company will continue in the tape manufacturing business, but will follow the businesses of its new primary asset backers.

The provisional agreement requires the approval of the Stock Exchange of Singapore, other authorities, creditors and shareholders, the managers said. A deadline of January 31, 1997 has been set for the deal to be signed.
